title: Texas A&M and Kentucky Face Off in SEC Season Opener
seoTitle: Texas A&M vs Kentucky SEC opener
subtitle: The historic matchup marks only the fourth game between the two football programs.
excerpt: Find out where to watch the Texas A&M vs Kentucky game, learn about the balanced history of the rivalry, and check the official broadcast details.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Texas A&M Aggies football team, ranked ninth, faces Kentucky this Saturday at 2:30 p.m. on their SEC season debut. The matchup is only the fourth time the two programs have met in history. The game will be played at Kyle Field in College Station and is expected to energize fans with a historically balanced rivalry.

Balanced Historical Rivalry

This Saturday’s duel is highly anticipated as it is only the fourth meeting in the teams’ history. Since the last encounter in 2018, the teams have not faced each other on the field. Currently, the Aggies lead the record with two wins to Kentucky’s one. However, the margin is narrow, as all prior games were decided by small point differentials. The largest point spread recorded was just six points, in Texas A&M’s overtime victory in the 2018 game.

The Game’s Venue in College Station

The weekend’s game will take place in College Station, marking the third time the two programs have played there. The venue will be Kyle Field, a stadium where the history shows a perfect balance between the competitors. Each team has already won a game on this turf, heightening expectations for a local showdown this Saturday. As the home team, the Texas A&M Aggies, ranked ninth, aim to use the home‑field advantage to open their SEC season with a win.

Official TV and Digital Broadcasts

For fans who want to watch the game live, the television broadcast will be on ESPN starting at 2:30 p.m. The TV crew will feature Joe Tessitore on play‑by‑play, Jesse Palmer as analyst, and Kris Budden doing field reporting. Viewers can tune in via various cable providers, including DirecTV, Dish Network, Comcast Xfinity, Spectrum, Verizon, Cox, and Optimum.

Radio and Spanish‑Language Options

The event’s coverage will also extend to radio through the Texas A&M Sports Network. The radio schedule starts early with the Spec’s 12th Man Tailgate Show at 12:30 p.m., followed by the Kickoff Show at 2:00 p.m. Local broadcast will be available on 1620 AM and 94.5 FM, plus SiriusXM satellite radio on channels 176 or 229, hosted by commentator Andrew Monaco, analyst Dave Elmendorf, and field reporter Will Johnson. Additionally, a Spanish broadcast will begin at 2:15 p.m. on La Jefa 102.7 FM and Radio Nuevo León in Monterrey, Mexico, narrated by Pedro Luna with commentary from Michael Gonzalez.

With information from Texas A&M Athletics.
